title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Boston Children's Hospital (2026)
summary: How to request medical records from Boston Children's Hospital in 2026: authorization forms, contact details, fees, portal access, and HIPAA rules for law firms.
body_markdown:
Requesting medical records from Boston Children's Hospital takes the right authorization form, correct contact information, and careful attention to HIPAA requirements. If you're an attorney building a personal injury case, incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or uninitialed sensitive-information categories can cause a request to be rejected or returned for correction, delaying retrieval.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers AI-powered retrieval that catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Boston Children's states that records are generally produced in[approximately 10 business days](https://www.childrenshospital.org/patients-families/you-arrive/your-visit/medical-records) after authorization is received. Separately, HIPAA generally requires action on qualifying patient access requests within 30 calendar days, with one permitted 30-day extension.


-


The standard authorization form asks the patient or representative to initial the sensitive-information categories they agree to have released, when that information is in the record.


-


The main Health Information Management (HIM) line for medical records is (617) 355-7546.


-


Radiology images use a separate authorization form and a different fax number than standard medical records.


-


The MyChildren's portal may not display the complete record, so litigation teams usually need a formal request.


-


Codes Health validates authorizations before submission and reports an average turnaround of a couple of weeks for complete records, with timing varying by provider responsiveness and request complexity.


## **Understanding Medical Records Request Forms and Your Rights**


### **What is a Medical Records Release Form?**


A medical records release form, also called an authorization for release of medical information, is the document that permits a healthcare provider to share protected health information with a designated recipient. HIPAA permits some disclosures without authorization, such as certain treatment, payment, healthcare operations, legally required, and judicial disclosures. But for a voluntary third-party request from an attorney that isn't otherwise permitted by HIPAA, Boston Children's generally needs a valid patient authorization or other lawful authority.


Boston Children's uses a two-page authorization form (Form 03038 Rev 4/18). Complete all fields that apply to your request. The form is available as an[English version](https://www.childrenshospital.org/sites/default/files/2026-08/medical-records-info-release-form-english.pdf) and a[Spanish version](https://www.childrenshospital.org/sites/default/files/media_migration/file_transfers/medical_records_info_release_form_spanish.pdf) .


### **Why is a HIPAA Release Form Necessary?**


The HIPAA Privacy Rule sets national standards for protecting individually identifiable health information. A covered entity like Boston Children's generally needs a written authorization when a disclosure isn't otherwise permitted or required by the Privacy Rule, which covers most attorney requests made on a client's behalf.


For legal matters, a signed authorization documents the patient's permission to share specific records with the named recipient.


### **Key Elements of a Valid Medical Records Release Form**


Boston Children's authorization form asks for:


**Patient Demographics:**


-


Full legal name (Last, First, Middle Initial)


-


Complete home address


-


Boston Children's Medical Record Number (if known)


-


Date of birth


-


Contact phone numbers and email


**Release Authorization:**


-


Recipient name and facility


-


Complete mailing address, phone, and fax


-


Purpose of release (Medical Care, School/Camp, Insurance, Personal, Legal Matter, or Other)


**Information Requested:**


-


Entire Medical Record with date range


-


Medical Record Abstract (History & Physical, Operative Report, Consults, Test Reports, Discharge Summary)


-


Pathology Materials with specific surgery dates


-


Other specified records


**Sensitive Information Authorizations:**


The form asks you to initial each sensitive category you agree to have released, if that information is in the patient's record:


-


HIV test results (with specific dates)


-


Genetic screening test results


-


Alcohol and drug abuse treatment records (protected under[42 CFR Part 2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-2) )


-


Mental health diagnosis and treatment


-


Confidential communications with licensed social workers


-


Sexually transmitted disease information


-


Hepatitis diagnosis and treatment


-


Pregnancy information


-


Abuse, neglect, domestic violence, and sexual assault counseling information


The form also separately addresses psychotherapy notes, which HIPAA treats differently from ordinary mental health records.


**Signature Requirements:**


Authorizations expire 12 months from the signature date unless you specify a different expiration. For patients under 18, a parent or legal guardian signs. The form states that information won't be released without a valid signature.


## **Directing Your Request: Contacting Boston Children's Hospital for Records**


### **Finding the Correct Department for Record Requests**


Boston Children's has a dedicated Health Information Management department for medical records requests. The medical records office is off-site and doesn't accommodate walk-ins.


**Main Medical Records Contact:**


-


**Phone:** (617) 355-7546


-


**Fax:** (617) 730-0327 or (617) 730-0329


-


**Email:** HIM-ROIStaff-dl@childrens.harvard.edu


-


**Mailing Address:** Attn: Medical Records, 300 Longwood Avenue, Boston, MA 02115


-


**Hours:** Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM


### **Other Department Contacts**


**For Radiology and Imaging Records:**


-


**Fax:** (617) 730-0538 (Department of Radiology Image Service Center), using the[radiology authorization form](https://www.childrenshospital.org/sites/default/files/media_migration/file_transfers/authorization_for_release_of_radiology_images.pdf)


**For Demographic Changes (Name, Date of Birth, or Sex):**


-


**Phone:** (617) 355-7544


-


**Fax:** (617) 730-4675


### **What Information to Prepare Before Contacting**


Before starting your request, gather:


-


Patient's full legal name and any aliases or prior names


-


Date of birth


-


Medical record number (if known)


-


Specific dates of service or admission dates


-


Identification or proof of authority when Boston Children's requires it for the request


-


Documentation of legal authority for guardians or other representatives


## **Submitting Your Medical Records Request to Boston Children's Hospital**


### **Step-by-Step Guide for Online Submission**


Boston Children's offers an electronic authorization option for patients, parents, legal guardians, and authorized representatives, linked from its[medical records page](https://www.childrenshospital.org/patients-families/you-arrive/your-visit/medical-records) . Healthcare professionals can use a separate paperless portal that uses email authentication instead of a login.


### **Required Documentation for Mail and Fax Requests**


When submitting by mail or fax, include:


-


The completed authorization form (both pages)


-


Identification or proof of authority when required for the request


-


Legal documentation if the signer is a guardian or other representative


-


Specific date ranges for the records needed


Send standard requests to (617) 730-0327 or (617) 730-0329, and keep your fax confirmation page for tracking.


### **Avoiding Delays: Common Submission Errors**


Requests are commonly rejected or returned for:


-


Missing signature or date on the authorization


-


Expired authorization (over 12 months old)


-


Needed sensitive-information categories not initialed


-


Inadequate patient identifiers for common names


-


Missing identification or proof of authority when required


-


Wrong recipient address or incomplete mailing information


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) uses AI-assisted validation to review requests before submission, checking authorizations, date ranges, and provider-specific requirements to catch these issues before they cause rejections.


## **Accessing Your Child's Medical Records Online: MyChart and Other Portals**


### **Setting Up MyChart Access for Your Child's Records**


Boston Children's uses the MyChildren's patient portal, powered by Epic MyChart. Parents of patients under 18 and patients 13 and older can access the portal, and the mobile app is available in English, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, and Simplified Chinese.


### **What Information Can You View Instantly?**


Through MyChildren's, authorized users can:


-


View health records and latest test results


-


Request school and camp forms


-


Send messages to the care team


-


Share health records with family members


-


Renew prescriptions and schedule appointments


-


Pay bills and update insurance information


### **Limitations of Online Portals for Comprehensive Records**


MyChildren's[terms of use](https://mychart.childrenshospital.org/mychart/Authentication/Login/StandardFile?option=TermsAndConditions) note that not all medical information may be accessible through the portal. If the records you need aren't available there, submit a formal medical record request using Boston Children's current electronic or paper options.


Psychotherapy notes are excluded from the standard HIPAA right of access. Firms that need certified or authenticated records should request the appropriate form of records for their proceeding rather than relying on portal downloads.


## **Navigating Requests for Old Medical Records from Boston Children's Hospital**


### **Specific Procedures for Archived Records**


Older records may not appear in the patient portal. Submit a formal request through the electronic option or the standard[authorization form](https://www.childrenshospital.org/sites/default/files/2026-08/medical-records-info-release-form-english.pdf) , specifying the exact date ranges needed.


### **Potential Challenges in Retrieving Very Old Records**


Massachusetts law requires hospitals to keep records for set retention periods, and older records may be stored off-site, so the hospital's 10-business-day estimate may run longer. HIPAA's 30-day access timeline still applies to qualifying patient requests for archived records.


### **Best Practices for Requesting Historical Data**


When requesting older records:


-


Include all available patient identifiers (medical record number, parent names for pediatric patients, and any other identifiers the form requests)


-


Specify exact date ranges rather than requesting "complete records"


-


Allow extra processing time for archived materials


-


Consider using[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) , which uses provider and facility data to identify where records may exist, especially useful for long medical histories or incomplete client recollection


## **Ensuring Completeness: What to Expect After Your Request**


### **Typical Turnaround Times for Medical Record Requests**


Boston Children's states that records are generally produced in approximately 10 business days after authorization is received. Separately, HIPAA generally requires action on a qualifying individual access request within 30 calendar days, with one permitted 30-day extension with written notice. Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 111, §70 has its own[30-day requirement](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXVI/Chapter111/Section70) , but it applies specifically to records requested to support Social Security or needs-based benefit claims and appeals.


**Suggested follow-up timeline:**


-


Day 7: Call (617) 355-7546 to confirm receipt


-


Day 10: Expected completion for standard requests


-


Day 15: Call HIM again if records haven't arrived


-


Day 20: Send a written status inquiry referencing the authorization date


### **Understanding Fees and Costs Associated with Copies**


**For Personal Requests:**


-


Boston Children's currently states that copies requested for personal reasons are charged[$6.50](https://www.childrenshospital.org/patients-families/you-arrive/your-visit/medical-records)


**For Healthcare Providers (Continuing Care):**


-


No charge


**For Attorneys and Insurers:**


-


Contact HIM at (617) 355-7546 to confirm the current fee schedule


-


Pricing is based on page count under Massachusetts regulations


**Massachusetts Hospital Fee Schedule (2024 Published Figures):**


The[2024 published schedule](https://mahima.memberclicks.net/ma-medical-record-copy-fees) set the following rates. Massachusetts permits annual CPI adjustments, so confirm the current figures before relying on them.


-


Base/Search Fee: $28.69


-


Pages 1 to 100: $0.96 per page


-


Pages 101 and up: $0.49 per page


### **How to Verify All Requested Records Have Been Provided**


When records arrive, check right away that:


-


All requested date ranges are covered


-


All specified record types are included


-


Pages are legible and complete


-


The correct patient name appears throughout


-


There are no duplicate or missing pages

## **HIPAA Compliance: Protecting Your Child's Protected Health Information**


### **Key Principles of the HIPAA Privacy Rule**


The HIPAA Privacy Rule requires covered entities to protect patient health information while giving individuals rights to access their own records. Key patient rights include:


-


Access to your own or your child's medical records


-


Requesting corrections to inaccurate records


-


Requesting an accounting of disclosures


-


Requesting confidential communications


-


Filing complaints about privacy violations


-


Revoking an authorization in writing (except where the hospital has already acted on it)


### **How Boston Children's Hospital Protects PHI**


Boston Children's maintains HIPAA compliance through:


-


Written authorization requirements for disclosures not otherwise permitted


-


A minimum necessary standard limiting shared information


-


Audit trails tracking record disclosures


-


Secure transmission methods for electronic records


-


Staff training on privacy requirements


### **Your Rights Under HIPAA Regarding Access and Amendments**


Under Boston Children's[Notice of Privacy Practices](https://www.childrenshospital.org/sites/default/files/2025-11/phi-privacy-notice-english.pdf) , you can ask Health Information Management to correct or amend health information you believe is incorrect or incomplete, and any denial will be explained in writing within 60 days. Changes to demographic details such as name, date of birth, or sex go through a separate process using the[demographic change form](https://www.childrenshospital.org/sites/default/files/media_migration/file_transfers/request_for_amendment_to_phi_form.pdf) and the (617) 730-4675 fax.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can I request my child's medical records if they are over 18 years old?**


Once a patient turns 18, they generally control their own medical records under HIPAA, and parents no longer have automatic access. The adult patient signs the authorization, or you'll need legal documentation, such as a healthcare power of attorney or guardianship, showing authority to act on their behalf.


### **What should I do if I believe my child's medical records are incomplete or incorrect?**


To correct or amend health information, contact Health Information Management under Boston Children's Notice of Privacy Practices. The hospital will explain any denial in writing within 60 days. For demographic changes like name, date of birth, or sex, use the separate demographic change form and fax it to (617) 730-4675.


### **How does Boston Children's Hospital handle records for deceased patients?**


For deceased patients, the executor or administrator of the estate generally signs the authorization, with documentation such as letters testamentary or letters of administration. A death certificate may also be required. Call HIM at (617) 355-7546 to confirm the documentation needed for your request.


### **Are there additional fees for receiving records on CD or in electronic format?**


Boston Children's currently states that copies requested for personal reasons cost $6.50. For attorneys and insurers, fees are based on page count under Massachusetts regulations, so confirm current pricing with HIM at (617) 355-7546. Radiology images on CD may carry separate charges.


### **Is it possible to track the status of my medical record request online?**


Boston Children's doesn't advertise public online tracking for standard authorization requests. Call (617) 355-7546 around business day seven to confirm receipt, then follow up again if records haven't arrived by day 15.
